title: Fields of definition of dynamical systems on $ mathbb{P}^{1}$. Improvements on a result of Silverman

predicted_errors.error_location: Proof of Lemma 4 (second paragraph, converse direction)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proof states: 'if σ ∈ Gal(K/k_ξ), then there exists f ∈ PGL₂(K) such that φ^σ = f ∘ φ ∘ f⁻¹ ... this implies that τ_σ ∘ f⁻¹ is an element of 𝒩_φ'. The composition order is wrong: from τ_σ φ τ_σ⁻¹ = f φ f⁻¹ one gets (f⁻¹τ_σ) φ (f⁻¹τ_σ)⁻¹ = f⁻¹(fφf⁻¹)f = φ, i.e. f⁻¹ ∘ τ_σ ∈ 𝒩_φ, whereas (τ_σ f⁻¹) φ (τ_σ f⁻¹)⁻¹ = τ_σ f⁻¹ φ f τ_σ⁻¹ need not equal φ. (Consistently, in the first direction the element of PGL₂ attached to f ∈ 𝒩_φ is h = τ_σ f⁻¹, so the inverse construction yields g = h⁻¹τ_σ = f⁻¹τ_σ.)

predicted_errors.error_location: Proof of Theorem 3, first bullet ('The fact that ξ descends to ℙ¹_K under the first condition…')
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Theorem 3 asserts descent to ℙ¹_{k_ξ}, but the proof states descent 'to ℙ¹_K', which is vacuously true (φ is given over K) and does not prove the theorem. The field should be the field of moduli k_ξ, not the algebraic closure K.

predicted_errors.error_location: §4, paragraph beginning 'Assume condition (2). The morphism 𝒫_ξ → P_ξ has degree d as well…'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The morphism from the stack 𝒫_ξ to its coarse space P_ξ is not a degree-d map; the sentence's own justification ('its base change to K̄ is the morphism ℙ¹/Aut → ℙ¹/Aut induced by φ') shows the intended object is the self-map P_ξ → P_ξ of the coarse space. Similarly the conclusion 'If d is even, then 𝒫_ξ(k_ξ) ≠ ∅ … hence we conclude by Lemma 11' is inconsistent, since Lemma 11 is stated in terms of P_ξ(k_ξ) ≠ ∅, not 𝒫_ξ(k_ξ).

predicted_errors.error_location: §4, sentence 'Furthermore, 𝒫_ξ is a Brauer–Severi curve over k_ξ, since its base change to K̄ is ℙ¹_K̄/Aut_K̄(φ)'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: This contradicts the immediately preceding sentence, which says only that 𝒫_ξ is *generically* a scheme (its base change being the quotient *stack* [ℙ¹/Aut]). The object whose base change is the quotient *scheme* ℙ¹/Aut, and which is the Brauer–Severi curve, is the coarse space P_ξ, not the stack 𝒫_ξ. The same paragraph later correctly distinguishes 𝒫_ξ(k_ξ) and P_ξ(k_ξ).

predicted_errors.error_location: § 'A remark about Silverman's results', displayed identification H¹(G_k, PGL₂(K)) = Br(k)[2]
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: H¹(G_k, PGL₂) classifies central simple algebras of degree 2 (quaternion algebras), i.e. Brauer classes of index dividing 2; this is in general a proper subset of Br(k)[2], since a class of period 2 may have index 4 or more. The stated equality (and likewise H¹(G_k, PGL₂(K̄)) = Br(k^p)[2]) is therefore false in general, even though the intended conclusion about the comparison map may still hold.

predicted_errors.error_location: §4, proof of Theorem 12 under condition (4) ('if char k ≠ 2, this is equivalent to saying that S has odd degree. We conclude that P(k_ξ) ≠ ∅')
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The equivalence between '|S(K̄)| odd' and 'deg S odd' is explicitly asserted only under char k ≠ 2, but the conclusion P(k_ξ) ≠ ∅ (which needs a closed subscheme of odd degree on a Brauer–Severi curve) is drawn unconditionally; in characteristic 2 an odd number of geometric points may have even degree, so the argument has a gap unless the stated condition includes char k ≠ 2.
